title: Freddy Fazbear's Pizza: The Sixth Hat
summary: At a birthday party at Freddy Fazbear's Pizza, a man in a Freddy suit led five children through the dining room, past Pirate Cove and behind the stage, and came out alone. He was charged, but the children were never found. Fazbear Entertainment bleached the floors, replaced the carpet and kept the band playing, until parents complained that the animatronics smelled and wept something dark from their eyes. Now the robots walk the halls after midnight, and the last night guard never finished his week.

characters.name: Ray Haskins, the Day Manager

art.description: heavyset man in his fifties with thinning hair, sweat-stained short-sleeved white dress shirt, crooked clip-on red tie, plastic name tag shaped like a cartoon bear's head reading RAY, holding a ring of keys
idle: glancing at his wristwatch, half turned toward his car, keys jangling in his other hand

dialogue: You're the new night guard? Great. Great! Okay. I gotta be gone by twelve, so listen fast.
The animatronics are left in free-roaming mode at night. Their servos lock up if they sit too long. So if they walk around, don't mind 'em.
Company policy, I gotta say it: Fazbear Entertainment is not responsible for damage to property or person.
If anything happens to an employee, a missing person report gets filed within ninety days. Or as soon as the place is bleached and the carpets are replaced.
Ha. Ha ha. ...Anyway.
The old night guard's probably still in the office. He never seems to go home. He'll walk you through it.
Whatever you hear on the stage, it's just the servos. It's always just the servos.
Here. Staff door, right side, under the light. Take it, take it. Twelve o'clock, I'm gone.
afterwards: I really gotta go. Good luck tonight, okay? Lock the door behind you.

characters.name: The Man on the Phone

art.description: ghost of a night guard slumped in a rolling swivel chair, rumpled navy security uniform torn at the shoulders, dark-stained collar, silver badge, navy cap pulled low shading his face so only a nervous smile shows, cheap headset around his neck, pale and faintly translucent
idle: slumped in the swivel chair, quite still

dialogue: Uh, hello? Hello, hello! Oh, you're, uh, actually here. Great. I-I wanted to give you a few words to get you settled in. I'm finishing up my last week now, actually.
So, the animatronics do get a bit quirky at night. Their servos lock up if they sit still too long, so they walk around. Totally normal.
Now, if one of them sees you after hours, it won't recognize you as a person. It'll see a bare metal endoskeleton without its costume on. That's against the rules here at Freddy Fazbear's Pizza.
So it'll try to, uh, forcefully stuff you inside a spare Freddy Fazbear suit. Which wouldn't be so bad, if the suits weren't full of crossbeams and wires. Uh. Yeah.
They used to walk around in the daytime too. Then there was the Bite of '87. It's amazing that the human body can live without the frontal lobe, you know?
Bonnie likes the West Hall closet. Chica hangs around the East Hall, by the kitchen. You'll hear her. The pans.
That west door's been jammed down since my, uh, my last night. The override key's pinned to the corkboard with the newspaper clippings, at the north end of the East Hall. East door's still up.
I'm gonna try to hold out until someone checks those suits in the back. Maybe it won't be so bad. Anyway. East Hall's right through there.
afterwards: Uh, that's, uh, all I've got for you. Good night!

props.name: cork bulletin board in a thin wooden frame, pinned thick with yellowed newspaper clippings with bold headlines
examine: Three yellowed clippings, pinned on top of each other. The headline of the first reads FIVE CHILDREN NOW REPORTED MISSING.
They were last seen following a man in a mascot costume into a back room during a birthday party. A suspect was charged. The children were never found.
PIZZERIA THREATENED WITH SHUTDOWN OVER SANITATION. Parents complain of a foul smell from the animatronics, with blood and mucus around their eyes and mouths.
One mother said the band looked like 'reanimated carcasses.'
The last one is short: LOCAL PIZZERIA SAID TO CLOSE BY YEAR'S END.
Something is pinned under the last clipping. A steel key on a red tag slips loose and clatters to the tile.
afterwards: FIVE CHILDREN NOW REPORTED MISSING. You already know the names. You only needed the one.

dialogue: Arr... OUT OF ORDER, they wrote. Since '87. Aye. Weren't me teeth, lass. Weren't me.
I seen it all from behind me curtain. Day o' the party, a Freddy come walkin' past me cove... five little mateys holdin' its paws.
Weren't Freddy, though. It walked wrong. Heavy on its heels, like a man. Its head sat crooked on its shoulders.
Up past the stage it took 'em. Toward the back, where the spare heads be kept. (the voice box skips, and a child whispers: 'it said there was more cake')
That Freddy come back alone, lass. Alone.
Grown-ups bleached the floors that week. Pulled up the carpet. But nobody ever cleared the birthday table. It be there still, in the big room.
The band smelled sweet after, lass. Sweet like a cake gone off.
Go and look at that table. Look at it fer me. I can't leave the cove.
afterwards: Arr... out of order, lass. Out of order.

intro.art: Freddy Fazbear's Pizza seen from across a wet, nearly empty parking lot at midnight: a low brown-brick building with grimy front windows. A tall pole sign shows a grinning cartoon bear in a top hat, its neon buzzing and half dead. One sodium streetlamp casts an orange pool on the cracked asphalt. A single sedan with its headlights on is parked near the side door, and thin mist hangs in the air. In one dark window, the faint pale shape of a face may be watching.
text: FREDDY FAZBEAR'S PIZZA. A magical place for kids and grown-ups alike. HELP WANTED: night security guard, 12 AM to 6 AM. $120 a week.

Six years ago your little brother Toby went to a birthday party here. He was seven. Five children followed a man in a mascot costume into a back room. The police charged a man. The children were never found.

Since then, parents have complained that the animatronics smell, and that something dark gathers around their eyes and mouths. The paper says the place will close by year's end. Nobody has ever searched it at night. So you took the job.
It's 11:52. The day manager is waiting by his car in the parking lot with the keys, and he looks like he wants to leave.
